content_units: Cape Town Internet Fit for Remote Work

For a remote worker with frequent video calls plus 3 people streaming,   reliability matters more than raw peak speed  . On your priorities—  reliability first, then value, then flexibility  —the best fit is   Fibre 100/50 Mbps  , with   Fibre 200/100 Mbps   as the runner-up.
Option Comparison Table
Option   Connection   Speed   Key Limits   Price   Contract/Flexibility   Fit for Your Use
Fibre 100/50   Fibre   100/50 Mbps   Uncapped   ZAR 799   Month-to-month   Strong balance of stable calls, multiple streams, and flexibility
Fibre 200/100   Fibre   200/100 Mbps   Uncapped   ZAR 999   12-month contract   Best performance headroom, but lower flexibility and higher cost
5G fixed wireless 80/20   5G Fixed Wireless   80/20 Mbps typical   1 TB fair-use   ZAR 699   Month-to-month   Cheapest and flexible, but less predictable for work-critical calls
Ranked Recommendation
Option 1:   Fibre 100/50 Mbps     Best overall for your priorities     Most balanced
- Fibre is typically more consistent than fixed wireless for video calls, latency, and evening congestion.
-   100/50 Mbps   is enough for one heavy remote worker and 3 concurrent streamers in most homes.
- At only   ZAR 200 less   than the faster fibre plan, it keeps strong reliability without locking you into a 12-month term.
- Month-to-month adds useful flexibility if you move, renegotiate, or upgrade later.
Option 2:   Fibre 200/100 Mbps     Best runner-up if you want more headroom     Highest performance
- Best choice if your household often does   simultaneous 4K streaming, large uploads, cloud backups, or multiple work devices  .
- The extra upload speed helps if you regularly send large files while on calls.
- Main trade-off:   12-month contract   and higher monthly cost reduce value/flexibility relative to Option 1.
Option 3:   5G fixed wireless 80/20 Mbps typical     Good budget alternative only     Lowest price
- 5G can perform well, but it is usually   less predictable than fibre   because speeds and latency can vary with signal quality and network load.
-   1 TB fair-use   may be enough for many homes, but a 4-person heavy-use household can approach it faster than expected with frequent HD/4K streaming, cloud sync, and downloads.
- Best only if budget and no-contract flexibility outweigh call stability.
Why Option 1 Wins on Your Priorities
-   Reliability first:   Fibre beats 5G fixed wireless for stable video meetings and lower performance swings.
-   Value next:   ZAR 799 for uncapped fibre is a strong middle ground; you avoid paying extra unless you truly need the added headroom.
-   Flexibility third:   Month-to-month is a meaningful advantage over a 12-month lock-in.
Practical Home-Use Readout
-   Video calls:   All 3 can work, but the two fibre options are safer for consistent call quality.
-   3 streamers at home:   Both fibre plans handle this comfortably; 5G may be fine but is more vulnerable at peak times.
-   Uploads and cloud work:   Option 2 is best, Option 1 is still solid, Option 3 is the weakest here.
-   Best overall:     Option 1
-   Runner-up:     Option 2
